newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechens say Russians force official plane to land.
newsitem.headline: Chechens say Russians force official plane to land.

text.p: Chechen officials accused the Russian military of forcing an airliner carrying the secessionist region's vice-president to turn back on a flight on Tuesday that would have taken him abroad, Russian media said.

Itar-Tass news agency and NTV commercial television quoted Vice-President Vakha Arsanov as saying Russian fighter jets had been scrambled to intercept him. Chechnya's first deputy prime minister, Movladi Udugov, was quoted as saying the incident was a "gross violation" of a peace treaty signed in Moscow last week.

Interfax news agency quoted Arsanov as saying he would give Russian government officials in Chechnya until noon (0800 GMT) on Wednesday to leave the region. No immediate reaction was available from the Russian authorities.
"This is a gross violation by the Russians," Arsanov told Reuters in Grozny. He said Russian officials had previously given him permission to fly to The Hague for an international conference.

Russian military operators had told the pilot of his plane to land at the south Russian town of Mineralniye Vody. Arsanov refused and turned back for the Chechen capital, Grozny. Two fighters accompanied the plane back to the Chechen frontier.

Udugov was quoted by Interfax as saying the incident was "a provocation aimed at wrecking the peace treaty", and said Chechnya would urge Russia to punish those involved. The Chechens have regularly complained that there is a "party of war" in Moscow which wants to prolong conflict in the region.
